clue.text: Sweetened spirit for Jerry's aged adversary

explanation.surface: A drink offered up to the elderly foe of a cartoon mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Tom and Jerry cartoons the cat Tom forever chases the mouse Jerry; an old version of that cat fits the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Tom is a slightly sweetened style of gin; the cartoon mouse's longtime foe is the cat, here an elderly one.

clue.text: The final part of a home game

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The deciding stage of a match played on the team's own ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end or last thing.

clue.text: Innards of hound, dead, foul intestines

indicators.note: foul suggests something fouled up, so the gathered letters are rearranged
innards are the inside parts, so take the letters between the first and last of the word hound

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of a dead dog's guts spilling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innards of' gives OUN, the middle of hound; 'foul' then rearranges OUN with DEAD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodena are the first sections of the small intestine, so the plural names intestines.

clue.text: Stay too long and get into the red?

explanation.surface: Lingering longer than you should and going into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as spending time over the limit; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending more time than allowed is overstaying; spending more money than you have puts your bank account into debt.

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word must be spoken to give the entry

parts.note: ossified means turned to bone, hence bony

explanation.surface: A wine described as stiff and lifeless, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: The French wine name is pronounced roughly 'bone', close to 'bony' as the setter hears it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a town in Burgundy whose name labels its red and white wines.

clue.text: Dallas matriarch coming up from Marseilles

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
from says the letters are taken out of the middle of the city name

explanation.surface: The head of a Texan family arriving from the French port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks EILLE out of Marseilles and 'coming up' turns it to give the answer. Miss Ellie Ewing was the matriarch in the US soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Ellie is the head of the Ewing family in the television drama set in Texas.

clue.text: With some misfortune, qualities are not fair

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lament that people's qualities, given some bad luck, are unjustly shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are unequal are uneven or unjust, so they lack fairness.

clue.text: Novelist-first of entrants,1, 760 yards ahead of Ms Budd

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the word entrants

parts.note: a mile is 1,760 yards
Zola Budd was a South African-born middle-distance runner who raced for Britain

explanation.surface: A race report: the leading runner a mile ahead of the barefoot athlete Budd.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray space in '1, 760' is a print quirk: read it as 1,760. Zola Budd famously ran barefoot in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was the French writer of Germinal and Nana, a famous author of fiction.

clue.text: Honeyed wine with rind of orange and lemon, returned

indicators.note: rind is the outer skin, so take the first and last letters of orange
returned means the word lemon is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sweet wine served with orange and lemon peel, then sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rind of' gives OE from orange and 'returned' turns lemon into NOMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenomel is an ancient Greek drink of wine mixed with honey, so it is sweetened with honey.

indicators.note: served suggests the letters are dished up in a new arrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A measure of liquor poured out for one, given with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges SINGLE with O to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloe gin is a liqueur made by steeping blackthorn berries in gin, so it is a spirit.

explanation.surface: A whodunnit offered up for people who catch mice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is Agatha Christie's long-running London stage whodunnit; the question mark flags the jokey second sense of a device that works on rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's murder play is a famous whodunnit, and a spring trap does its work on mice.

clue.text: Wine from friend with American flower-girl

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
US is short for American, as in United States
Rose is both a flower and a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bottle brought by a pal accompanied by a US bridesmaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower-girl' looks like a wedding bridesmaid but is one word that is both a bloom and a female name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mateus Rosé is a popular Portuguese pink wine sold in a distinctive flask-shaped bottle.

indicators.note: some says only part of the word house-red is needed, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A bit of the cheap wine set aside for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' here means someone who employs a thing, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes use of something employs it, so a person who employs a tool uses it.

indicators.note: spilt suggests the bread tumbling about, so its letters are rearranged
missing says one piece is taken away from the rearranged letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Wine and loaves knocked over at a party of fifty, with some gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes L, the Roman 50, from LOAVES, and 'spilt' rearranges the remaining OAVES to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white Italian wine named after a town near Verona.

parts.note: squash is a British fruit cordial, a sweet syrup diluted with water

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of gin are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit cordial and gin blended into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, squash is a concentrated fruit drink diluted with water. 'mixed' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushing or quashing an uprising means putting it down, so to quell is to suppress.

clue.text: Wine upset — no citrus fruits left in

indicators.note: upset means the whole sequence of letters is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left is placed inside the fruit

parts.note: limes are small green citrus fruits

explanation.surface: A bottle knocked over because there was no fruit left in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives LLIMES; with NO in front that is NOLLIMES, and 'upset' turns the whole run over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sémillon is a golden-skinned grape used for white wines such as Sauternes, and the name labels those wines.

clue.text: Spanish girl embraced Spanish boy for drug

indicators.note: embraced says one name holds the other inside it

parts.note: Maria is a common Spanish girl's name
Juan is a common Spanish boy's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish couple's hug, told as a romance with a drug twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced' sets the boy's name between the fourth and fifth letters of the girl's.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis smoked for its intoxicating effect is a narcotic, an illegal substance in many countries.

indicators.note: backed means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a cadet is a young trainee in the forces

explanation.surface: A wine trouble supported by a new army trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reads SUM backwards to give MUS; 'by' is a link joining it to CADET.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley in France.

parts.note: to chime is to ring like a bell
RA stands for Royal Academician, a British artist

explanation.surface: A whim to telephone a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an impossible dream or illusion, a fantastic notion.

clue.text: Wine or port. Yes — in Germany

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, known as Rio
ja is the German word for yes

explanation.surface: Choosing between wine and port, answered in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the second drink, but here it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine from the region of that name.

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters relocate, so to Basel is rearranged

explanation.surface: Monks relocating to the Swiss city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblates are lay people dedicated to religious life, often attached to a monastery.

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling movement, so the letters of the words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A simple statement about a sparkling drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' seems to describe the drink but signals the rearrangement of IT'S A.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is an Italian sparkling white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Wine is usable when mixed with most of 18

indicators.note: mixed means all the gathered letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of says one letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: 18 refers to the answer at 18 across, a Spanish red

explanation.surface: A wine becomes drinkable when blended with a Spanish red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims RIOJA to IOJA; 'when mixed with' rearranges USABLE and IOJA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaujolais is a light red wine from the region of Burgundy in France.

indicators.note: right away says the abbreviation for right is taken off

parts.note: a bracer is a stiffening drink of spirits

explanation.surface: Offering support by downing a stiff drink immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it tells you to remove R from BRACER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a prop or strut holding something up.

indicators.note: almost says the word falls just short, losing one letter

explanation.surface: A building order nearly famous enough to be iconic.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first C from ICONIC to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionic order is one of the classical column types, with scroll-shaped capitals.

explanation.surface: A mixed drink that also fixes onto a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a brandy, orange liqueur and lemon drink, and also a passenger car fitted to a motorcycle.

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Downing a single mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb for drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a mixed drink of gin and vermouth.

explanation.surface: A drink served for burials.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense names places of burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux region whose name labels its wines; tombs are dug for burying the dead.

clue.text: White wine at public houses on account

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the first piece before the second

parts.note: bars are places serving drinks, like pubs

explanation.surface: White wine bought at the pub and put on the tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is just a link; 'on' in an across clue means the account abbreviation follows the drinking places.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.
